$comment: Single source of truth for @aihu/use's family subpaths (ratified architecture: CORE stays dependency-free; FAMILY subpaths may declare optional peers, isolated per-composable entry). Consumed by scripts/dep-check.ts (subpath purity + peer ownership), scripts/check-use-registry-parity.ts (family-aware parity), and scripts/gen-use.ts (the --family scaffolder). A family entry here is a deliberate, reviewed edit — never a scaffolder side effect (see scripts/gen-use.ts validateFamily). Declaring a family (and its eventual peer map) ahead of its first member is intentional: it fixes the shape so 150 authors can't improvise a different one, and it costs nothing at the npm level because no peerDependencies/devDependencies are added until a real composable claims a peer (see dep-check.ts's 'active peer' scoping).

motion.$comment: aggregateLimit raised 3 KB -> 6 KB in wave 2 (Slice 8, Tier-C canvas infrastructure) against a MEASURED aggregate of 5314 B — not a reactive bump-until-green. Wave 1's five text/timer members totalled ~1.8 KB; useCanvasSurface (2090 B) + useCharacterField (2932 B) + useParticleField (3545 B) share the surface chunk, so the deduplicated aggregate is 5314 B, leaving 830 B (~14%) of headroom under 6 KB. memberLimit deliberately STAYS at 900 B: it only seeds the .size-limit.json row a new composable seeds with, and the family's typical member is still a sub-1 KB text/timer composable — the three canvas members carry per-row limits measured individually instead, so a future small composable is not handed a 4 KB budget by default.
